scope.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: n and m are integers with n≥1 and m≥1 (represented as natural-number dimensions).
u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth: every finite-order coordinate partial derivative exists and is continuous on this open domain.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0, |u(x,r)|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0 there exists a real scalar a with u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r). No regularity or globally chosen scalar field is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C_[s,t]⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C_[s,t] and every r∈[s,t].

source.statement: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

correspondence.explanation: The parameters n,m:ℕ with H001 express precisely positive integer dimensions; Fin indices reindex 1,...,n. W m has exactly the source Euclidean norm and dot product; V n has the same coordinate topology and product Lebesgue measure. A source u on V×(0,∞) extends by zero to V×ℝ and any total u restricts back; agreement on an open neighborhood of each positive-time point preserves every displayed derivative, smoothness, sphere condition, pointwise existential normality and compact support locally uniformly over each [s,t]. Thus H002 is equivalent to source joint smoothness on this open finite-dimensional real domain; H003/H004 are unit-vector conditions, H005 preserves the pointwise scalar existential with no regularity assumption, and H006 quantifies the same single compact C for the entire positive interval. In both directions restriction/extension preserves the density and its spatial integrals at positive times. The conclusion asserts absolute Lebesgue integrability, differentiability on the open half-line and zero ordinary derivative everywhere there, together with constancy between arbitrary positive s,t. energy unfolds to the exact norm-square sum integral with no 1/2; integrability is explicitly proved rather than inferred from the total integral notation. No statement is made at nonpositive times.
